page.layout: One printed page: page number at the head, then a centred heading and a verse poem in six stanzas of four lines. No running head, catchword or signature. The faint printing at the right edge belongs to the neighbouring page and is not transcribed.

main_text.head: Alia regula uitæ, à Paulo Chierle[?]ro Elsterb.
main_text.p: Vt tibi toto Rideat æuo Vita beatæ Plena salutis:
Exue culpam, Indue Christum, Dilige casto Numen amore.
Postea cauta Mente caueto, Ne tibi pectus Occupet error.
Ritè labore Fungere iusso: Auspice Christo Perfice cuncta.
Sors ubi tristis Venerit olim, Pectora uerbi Robore fulci.
Sic tibi dulcis Vita fauebit, Aurea donec Ibis ad astra.

page.notes: The heading's second line reads "ro Elsterb." after a line break at "Chierle-". The first letters of "Chierle" are partly obscured by a stain, so the reading is doubtful. Italic and roman type in the verse is not clearly distinguishable on the scan and is given in plain type. A small mark near "Sors" and a dark spot near "Pectora" are stains, not printed text.
